title: Philidor's Legacy
subtitle: The immortal smothered mate: double check, queen sac, Nf7#.
goals: Drive the king into the corner with checks
Use double check — the unanswerable weapon
Sacrifice the queen for the smothered finish

steps.say: Described by Philidor in 1749 (and known even before him), this is the most famous combination in chess: queen and knight drive the enemy king into the corner, the queen sacrifices herself to seal the last exit with Black's OWN rook, and the knight — the one piece that attacks over walls — mates a king smothered by his own army. Note Black even threatens ...Qxg5: every move of the machine is a check, so the threat never lands.

steps.prompt: Warm up at the finish line: the king is cornered and boxed in. Queen sac, then mate — two moves!
hints: The g8 square is the king's only air. Give your queen there — Black's rook MUST take, sealing the corner shut.
Qg8+!! Rxg8, and now the knight strikes the square only knights can reach.

line.say: The immortal sacrifice — and Rxg8 is forced: the king cannot capture, because your h6 knight guards g8.
Smothered mate. The king suffocates behind his own rook and pawns while the knight checks from f7 — the one attack no wall can block.

rejections.say: Check — but the king slips out through g8! The queen must SEAL that square first, by dying on it: Qg8+!! forces the rook to become its own king's tombstone.

steps.wrongSay: The king needs g8. Give your queen on that exact square — the recapture builds the tomb.
steps.successSay: Qg8+!! Rxg8, Nf7# — the two-move finish. Now earn it from further out.

steps.prompt: The complete Philidor's Legacy: nine forced moves from a quiet-looking position. Begin with the check on the long diagonal!
hints: Qc4+ seizes the a2–g8 diagonal with check. The king must step to the corner — and f7 belongs to your knight next.
Then the knight machine: Nf7+, Nh6+ DOUBLE CHECK, back to Kh8 — and the queen gives herself on g8.

line.say: Check on the a2–g8 diagonal. The king must step into the corner...
The knight fork-checks from f7 — the king returns to g8, hoping for peace...
DOUBLE CHECK — knight from h6, queen down the diagonal. Both at once: no block, no capture can answer two attackers. Only a king move...
...and now the immortal queen sacrifice. Guarded by your knight, she cannot be taken by the king — the rook must do it...
PHILIDOR'S LEGACY. The rook Black was forced to place on g8 smothers his own king; the knight mates through the wall. 1749 called — you played it perfectly.

rejections.say: Without the queen check first, the king isn't in the corner — Black just plays ...Rxf7 or walks away. Every move of this machine is a check; start with Qc4+.

steps.wrongSay: Nine moves, every white move a check or a mate. The first check comes down the a2–g8 diagonal.
steps.successSay: King hunt, double check, queen sac, smothered mate — the full Legacy. This is the combination every chess player wants to play once in their life. You're ready for your chance.

steps.prompt: Prove you know the machine's soul: replay the hunt up to the DOUBLE check — the move greedier players get wrong.
hints: From f7 the knight could grab material — but the double check is worth more than any rook.
Nh6+ — the ONLY move that checks with both pieces at once.

line.say: Fork-check — and here stands the moment of temptation...
Double check! Greed would have grabbed the a8 rook and let the king escape. The double check keeps him chained to the corner — mate follows in two.

rejections.say: No check — and ...Rxf7 simply eats the knight. Philidor's machine runs on checks: the queen fires down the diagonal first.

steps.wrongSay: Re-run the machine: diagonal check, knight check, DOUBLE check.
steps.successSay: The discipline of the double check — material means nothing while the machine runs. Lesson complete.
